- [2026-05-13-claude-cli-jsonl-is-superset-of-wire.md](2026-05-13-claude-cli-jsonl-is-superset-of-wire.md) — 2026-05-13: The claude CLI's session JSONL on disk is a **superset** of its stream-json wire output to consumers. Live capture proved: for a mid-turn queued-message scenario, stdout carries `assistant/user/system/result/control_response/rate_limit_event` and NOTHING else; the JSONL adds `attachment`, `queue-operation`, `queued_command` (top-level), `last-prompt`, `direct`, `deferred_tools_delta`, `mcp_instructions_delta`, `skill_listing`, `hook_success`. Stream-json is the **interactive contract**; JSONL is the **resumability snapshot**. **Never synthesize wire baselines** from JSONL persistence or from binary string-dumps — always FORGE_WIRE_CAPTURE-equivalent live-capture first. Bit forge PR #117: dimmed mid-turn bubbles stayed dimmed forever because the "wire echo" I designed against doesn't exist on the wire (only in JSONL). Live un-dim must hook turn boundaries; session-resume rendering must read JSONL directly. Generalises to any wrapper around the `claude` CLI (forge-sdk, claude-agent-sdk, architect, claudechic).
- [2026-05-13-git-init-b-requires-2-28.md](2026-05-13-git-init-b-requires-2-28.md) — 2026-05-13: `git init -b <branch>` (set initial branch on init) was added in git 2.28 (Jul 2020). On older runners (Ubuntu 20.04 ships **git 2.25.1**) the flag exits 129 with `error: unknown switch 'b'`, no `.git` is created, every subsequent command fails with `fatal: not a git directory`, and dependent tests appear to fail downstream — not at the actual init step. Portable replacement: `git init -q` then `git symbolic-ref HEAD refs/heads/<branch>` (works on every git version). Also: `.output().expect("git ok")` ONLY catches spawn failures — non-zero exits return `Ok(Output)`, so test-setup git commands MUST `assert!(status.success(), ...)` or the failure surfaces at a downstream assertion with no breadcrumb. Bit forge PR #113. Generalises to any project where tests spin up tempdir git repos and CI runs an older Linux distro.
- [2026-05-11-shell-pipe-loses-upstream-exit-code.md](2026-05-11-shell-pipe-loses-upstream-exit-code.md) — 2026-05-11: A shell pipeline `cmd | grep -v noise` reports grep's exit code, not `cmd`'s — wrapper scripts that pipe through cosmetic filters silently lose upstream failures. Bit `ws nix apply` on dotfiles: when activate's `brew bundle` hit a Homebrew internal bug and exited non-zero, the wrapper printed `Applied.` in green and the user-facing config symlinks were left at the previous generation (machine running an older config than the Nix store had registered). Fixes: zsh `${pipestatus[1]}`, bash `${PIPESTATUS[0]}`, or `set -o pipefail` at script top. Applies to any wrapper piping `darwin-rebuild` / `nix` / CI build output / `cargo` / `go build` / `make` through grep/sed/awk for noise reduction.
- [sonarr-app-sync-needs-tv-category.md](sonarr-app-sync-needs-tv-category.md) — 2026-05-08: Sonarr's `ApplicationIndexerSync` silently skips a Prowlarr indexer when its `categorymappings` has zero `TV/*` (Newznab `5xxx`) entries — even when `caps.modes.tv-search: [q, season, ep]` is declared. Pair with the cap-filter TIL: an indexer needs BOTH a TV-cap mode AND a TV-category mapping to make it through to Sonarr; declaring only one isn't enough. Diagnose by comparing `.capabilities.categories | map(.id)` of the broken indexer vs a working sibling. Applies to any custom Cardigann YAML where the underlying site mixes movies + TV in forums.
- [2026-05-08-formfield-taffy-over-tui-framework.md](2026-05-08-formfield-taffy-over-tui-framework.md) — 2026-05-08: When a reactive Rust TUI framework tempts you, lift the two ideas it actually solves — a small `FormField<T>` helper (value, is_dirty, is_valid, error; ~50–100 LoC, no deps) plus **direct** `taffy` calls for any genuinely-Flexbox surface (footer chip rows, multi-column dialogs, status headers) — instead of adopting the framework whole. Avoids paying the framework tax on the streaming-render parts of the codebase that don't benefit. Heuristic: if a framework would help < 50% of your surface area, lift the helpful ideas as small in-house helpers and skip the framework. Generalises beyond TUIs to any UI framework adoption call.
- [2026-05-08-reactive-tui-fits-forms-not-streaming.md](2026-05-08-reactive-tui-fits-forms-not-streaming.md) — 2026-05-08: Reactive component frameworks fit **form-shaped** TUI (settings dialogs, autocomplete, list-and-select, prompts, wizards) — signals + derived memos + diff-and-paint compose cleanly there. They fight **streaming-render** TUI (chat / log / append-mostly with per-item line caches): the render hot path uses an imperative *render-time stamp* pattern (each interactive element writes `(y_offset, height)` back onto its own state during paint, so the click handler does an interval check later) which a declarative diff loop fights directly — stamps go stale, re-renders skip, hit-testing breaks. Diagnostic: if your render hot path writes back to widget state during paint, you're streaming-shaped and any "adopt a reactive framework" pitch deserves suspicion. Apply reactive ideas to the form-shaped islands; keep the streaming spine imperative.
- [emby-providerids-silently-ignored.md](emby-providerids-silently-ignored.md) — 2026-05-08: Emby `Items?ProviderIds=Tmdb.X` is silently ignored — returns the entire library, and naive `.Items[0]` reads always pick the alphabetically-first title (`#Single` in our hub). Use `?AnyProviderIdEquals=tmdb.X` (singular param, lowercase provider key). Diagnostic: `TotalRecordCount` equals library size instead of `1`, and every distinct TMDB resolves to the same Item ID. Bit a bulk favoriting script that reported all 15 movies as `already-fav (306083)`. Same shape almost certainly applies to Jellyfin (forked from Emby).
- [2026-05-08-cardigann-caps-must-claim-season-ep.md](2026-05-08-cardigann-caps-must-claim-season-ep.md) — 2026-05-08: Cardigann YAML for Prowlarr/Jackett: declaring narrowed `tv-search` `supportedParams` (e.g. `[q]` only, dropping `season,ep`) makes Sonarr's `ReleaseSearchService` **silently exclude** the indexer from `/release?episodeId=X` queries — no error, no log, just missing from the queried set. Caps must claim full `[q, season, ep]` even if you only want to use `q` internally; use `keywordsfilters` regex `["\\bS\\d+E\\d+\\b", ""]` to strip Cardigann's auto-injected `SxxExx` so the URL stays keyword-only. Bonus: Prowlarr's per-indexer `tags` field is also a sync filter — if Sonarr's app config has `tags: [N]`, only indexers tagged with N get pushed by `ApplicationIndexerSync`. Untagged custom indexer = silent skip. Diagnostic shape: indexer DB row has all flags green, but Sonarr's "Searching indexer(s)" log lines never include it AND no entry in Prowlarr's `ApplicationIndexerMapping`.
- [2026-05-08-ghostty-option-arrow-readline-esc.md](2026-05-08-ghostty-option-arrow-readline-esc.md) — 2026-05-08: Ghostty with `macos-option-as-alt = true` (and even with kitty enhanced keyboard negotiated) emits **legacy readline ESC sequences** for Option+Arrow — Option+Right arrives as `Char('f')+ALT`, Option+Left as `Char('b')+ALT`, NOT the kitty CSI `Right/Left + ALT` shape. Option+Backspace/Delete DO arrive as kitty CSI. Cmd+Shift+Z arrives as `Char('z') + SUPER|SHIFT`, not `Char('Z') + SUPER`. Apps porting upstream Linux-first key handlers must match BOTH shapes for macOS-native word-nav / redo. Plus zellij's default `bind "Alt f" { ToggleFloatingPanes; }` swallows the ESC+f passthrough before it reaches the inner app — needs `unbind "Alt f"` and friends. Existing zellij sessions cache keybinds at start; reload requires fresh session. Diagnostic: a 30-line standalone crossterm reader to capture actual `KeyEvent` shapes beats documentation.
- [2026-05-06-zonky-portable-postgres-binaries.md](2026-05-06-zonky-portable-postgres-binaries.md) — 2026-05-06: When CI tests need a real PG binary on PATH (pgtemp / embedded-postgres), distro packages are flaky — PGDG retired `focal-pgdg`, Docker-image extracts hit libicu version mismatches across Ubuntu LTS. Use zonky's `embedded-postgres-binaries-linux-amd64` JAR from Maven Central — single self-contained tarball bundles libicu/libssl/libcrypto/etc., works on any glibc Linux. ~14 MB, idempotent install, must set `LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$PG_HOME/lib` for bundled libs. Origin: aware → busytools transfer.
- [2026-05-06-github-transfer-runner-regs-zombie.md](2026-05-06-github-transfer-runner-regs-zombie.md) — 2026-05-06: GitHub repo transfer carries pre-existing self-hosted runner registrations along as **repo-scoped runners at the new owner**. Containers using `EPHEMERAL: "true"` only deregister *after* a job completes — not on container shutdown — so swapping to an org-scoped pool by stopping the old containers leaves stranded `offline` zombie registrations on `repos/<org>/<repo>/actions/runners`. Harmless (no jobs route to offline runners), GitHub auto-prunes after ~14 days, OR delete via repo Actions UI. Permission gotcha: a fine-grained PAT with org-level "Self-hosted runners: R/W" cannot delete REPO-scoped runners under that org (returns 404) — they're separate permission spaces. Diagnose by hitting `/repos/<org>/<repo>/actions/runners` post-swap and checking `total_count > 0`.
- [2026-05-05-revert-and-file-audit-when-premise-flagged-stale.md](2026-05-05-revert-and-file-audit-when-premise-flagged-stale.md) — 2026-05-05: When the user flags an edit's foundational premise as stale ("this whole framing is suspect", "no longer holds", "outdated"), the right move is to **revert and file an audit issue** — not polish the wording or argue the original framing. Refining a wrong-premise edit compounds the error. Sequence: (1) revert to a generic non-claiming version, (2) file an audit issue capturing what the user flagged + what verification is needed (wire captures, repro conditions), (3) move on to other work. Don't try to fix the audit in the same session — it deserves focused attention with proper data. Symptom: you're polishing language while the code path it describes might not even fire anymore. Forge#41 (rate-limit `EXTRA_USAGE_REQUIRED_MESSAGE` audit) is a clean example of the audit-issue shape.
- [2026-05-05-read-code-before-brainstorming-architecture.md](2026-05-05-read-code-before-brainstorming-architecture.md) — 2026-05-05: For any architectural question in a non-trivial codebase, **`grep` comes before `AskUserQuestion`**. Default mental model: "anything I'm about to propose has high prior probability of already being designed and committed." Wasted user time today brainstorming a forge-daemon revival from scratch — proposing JSON-RPC protocols, transport choices, multi-client semantics, reverse-RPCs — when the daemon already had ALL of that built (registry.rs `HashMap<SessionId, _>`, `multi_client.rs::claim_primary`, `reverse_rpc.rs`). User pushback: "questions u asked are already solved in daemon no?" Symptoms: sketching clean-slate architecture for an existing subsystem, asking the user to choose paradigms the codebase already committed to, mentioning a component by name and asking "how should we build it" instead of "what does it currently do." Prescription: 5 minutes of `find` + `grep` first, state what exists in your response, reserve `AskUserQuestion` for genuinely-open decisions only.
- [2026-05-04-tracing-subscriber-envfilter-literal-targets.md](2026-05-04-tracing-subscriber-envfilter-literal-targets.md) — 2026-05-04: `tracing-subscriber::EnvFilter` directives match the event's literal `target`, not the crate name. When a `tracing::debug!` macro sets `target: "app.session"` explicitly, a directive `forge_tui=debug` doesn't prefix-match — falls through to default level, which is **OFF** when no bare-level directive is present (e.g. `forge_tui=debug,tui_markdown=info` has no leading `info,`). Silent drop. Fix: `--log-filter app=debug` matches all `app.*` literals; or use `--diagnostics-preset session` which expands to `info,bridge.lifecycle=debug,bridge.protocol=debug,app.session=debug,...` (leading `info,` makes the default `info` so `logging_initialized` info line ALSO fires — sanity check). Generalises to any Rust crate using `tracing` with explicit `target:` literals over module-path defaults.
- [2026-05-04-account-scoped-api-quota-vs-config-dir-isolation.md](2026-05-04-account-scoped-api-quota-vs-config-dir-isolation.md) — 2026-05-04: forge showed "Approaching rate limit, 102%" on a fresh launch under `~/.claude-nf` despite no on-disk forge cache. First instinct was "CLI subprocess caches headers outside `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`." Wrong — wire breadcrumb under two different Anthropic accounts produced wholly different payload shapes (`overage @ utilization 1.02` vs `five_hour @ allowed`), proving the state is account-scoped on Anthropic's side, not config-dir-scoped. Diagnostic playbook: when a CLI/TUI shows seemingly-stale quota state on fresh launch under an isolated config-dir, capture the wire payload first (don't go straight to "find the local cache"), then reproduce under a DIFFERENT account (not just a different config-dir). Same payload across accounts → genuine local cache. Different payload → account-scoped, working as designed. Applies to any auth-API wrapper (Anthropic, OpenAI, GitHub, Slack, AWS, etc.).
- [2026-05-04-sonarr-tvsearch-indexer-side-parsing.md](2026-05-04-sonarr-tvsearch-indexer-side-parsing.md) — 2026-05-04 (workarounds corrected 2026-05-06): Sonarr's tvsearch hits per-app endpoints with `&season=N&ep=M` filters; indexers run their OWN parser to TV-tag releases, and titles like `2026x29` (vs `S2026E29`) fail that pre-parse — invisible to tvsearch despite high seeders. Symptom: 0-result auto-search; generic `type=search` finds it instantly. **Real workaround**: Sonarr's UI Interactive Search does NOT bypass tvsearch (verified, both call `/release?episodeId=X` which returns 0 too). Bypass at qBittorrent level: Prowlarr generic search → grab `magnetUrl` → POST to qBit's `/api/v2/torrents/add` with `category=<sonarr-tv>` + `savepath=/downloads`. Sonarr's downloads handler imports based on filename parsing (must match TVDB's episode numbering — Sprint releases using `2026x37` for E27 fail this and need manual-import). Bonus: Sonarr's `alternateTitles` is read-only — TVDB-synced, `PUT /api/v3/series/{id}` returns 202 but silently drops edits.
- [2026-05-03-zerodha-kite-enctoken-broken-routes.md](2026-05-03-zerodha-kite-enctoken-broken-routes.md) — 2026-05-03: Zerodha Kite's unofficial enctoken auth flow (login-cookie scrape, no paid API key) breaks `kc.ltp()` (400 Bad Request) and `kc.instruments()` (Route not found), but `kc.historical_data(token, ...)` works fine when given a real instrument_token. Workaround: the public CSV dump at `https://api.kite.trade/instruments/NSE` requires NO auth, lists every NSE instrument with `tradingsymbol → instrument_token`, and is stable for years. Cache to disk, refresh weekly, fall back to stale cache on network failure (tokens don't churn). Pairs with NSE public quote API for live LTP. NIFTY 50 token = 256265, hard-code it. Applies to any project using `kiteconnect` without the paid Connect subscription, in any language.
- [2026-05-03-sqlite-fk-toggle-table-rebuild.md](2026-05-03-sqlite-fk-toggle-table-rebuild.md) — 2026-05-03: SQLite can't `ALTER TABLE ADD CONSTRAINT`; rebuild via CREATE NEW → INSERT → DROP OLD → RENAME. If other tables hold FKs to the rebuilt table, `DROP TABLE` fails with `FOREIGN KEY constraint failed` under `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON`. Fix: toggle `foreign_keys=OFF` BEFORE any `BEGIN` (PRAGMA is a no-op inside a transaction), wrap the rebuild in `try`/`finally`, run `PRAGMA foreign_key_check` between rebuild and re-enable to catch orphans loudly, restore `ON` in `finally`. Idempotency probe via `sqlite_master.sql LIKE '%new-marker%'` to short-circuit on already-migrated DBs. Recreate dropped indexes inside the rebuild script. Backfill non-conforming rows BEFORE rebuild so the new CHECK accepts everything.
- [2026-04-27-borrowed-gh-token-must-match-git-identity.md](2026-04-27-borrowed-gh-token-must-match-git-identity.md) — 2026-04-27: When the current project lacks its own `GH_TOKEN` and you need to borrow one from another project's `.envrc` (via `direnv exec`), the source project's `git config user.email` MUST match the current project's. Different `user.email` = different GitHub account = release/API call attributed to the wrong identity even if it succeeds. Never fall back to user/global-scope token as a "close enough" alternative — that may also be the wrong account. Near-miss: tried to use `granite-backend`'s `hackercf` token to cut a `vedhavyas/claude-code-proxy` release. Compare `user.email` across the two repos before borrowing; if no match exists on disk, escalate to user instead of silently picking one.
- [2026-04-26-bash-set-e-suspended-via-or-and-subshells.md](2026-04-26-bash-set-e-suspended-via-or-and-subshells.md) — 2026-04-26: `func || rc=$?` and `( func ) || rc=$?` BOTH suspend `set -e` for the entire function/subshell body in bash — internal failures get silently swallowed. Subshell wrap does NOT escape it (bash dynamic-scopes the suspension; subshell inherits parent's "in `||` context" state). Verified empirically. Fixes: drop `||` capture entirely, OR `bash -c 'set -euo pipefail; func' || rc=$?`, OR explicit `|| return $?` per fallible line. Diagnostic: script reports exit 0 but journal shows internal commands clearly failing.
- [2026-04-26-macos-ssh-usekeychain-non-gui-shells.md](2026-04-26-macos-ssh-usekeychain-non-gui-shells.md) — 2026-04-26: macOS encrypted SSH keys fail in non-GUI shells (SSH'd-in sessions, launchd jobs, CI) with `Permission denied (publickey)` — `ssh -vT` shows `Server accepts key:` then signing silently fails. Cause: launchd's per-user `ssh-agent` only exports `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` into the GUI login session; new sessions don't inherit it. Fix: declarative `UseKeychain yes` in SSH config — has the SSH client read the passphrase directly from Keychain, bypassing the agent. Prereq: `ssh-add --apple-use-keychain <key>` was run once interactively to store the passphrase. Diagnostic shape "Server accepts key + Permission denied" generalises to any platform = client can't sign = encrypted key + no agent/keychain access in this context.
- [2026-04-26-github-public-keys-endpoint.md](2026-04-26-github-public-keys-endpoint.md) — 2026-04-26: `curl -s https://github.com/<user>.keys` returns the user's public SSH auth keys with no auth required — perfect for "is this key actually registered?" diagnostic. Pipe through `ssh-keygen -lf /dev/stdin` per line to get fingerprints comparable to local `ssh-keygen -lf id_ed25519.pub`. Pairs with `ssh -vT` (`Server accepts key:` line) to disambiguate "key isn't registered" vs "key is registered but signing fails".
- [2026-04-25-home-manager-symlink-staleness.md](2026-04-25-home-manager-symlink-staleness.md) — 2026-04-25: Home-Manager-managed files run from `~/.config/.../foo` → `/nix/store/<hash>-home-manager-files/...` symlinks frozen at last activation. `bash path/in/repo/foo.sh` testing the new behavior proves nothing about what the menu bar / launchd loads. Diagnostic: `shasum -a 256` repo vs ~ + `readlink` the deployed path. Fix: `ws nix apply` (or `home-manager switch`, `darwin-rebuild switch`, `stow -R`, `chezmoi apply`). Same trap applies to any content-addressed store / symlink-materialized config system.
- [home-manager-zsh-session-vars-guard.md](home-manager-zsh-session-vars-guard.md) — 2026-04-24: Long-lived shells can inherit `__HM_ZSH_SESS_VARS_SOURCED=1`, causing new Home Manager session vars to never appear until the parent terminal tree is restarted.
- [2026-04-23-zsh-async-status-ansi-rewrite.md](2026-04-23-zsh-async-status-ansi-rewrite.md) — 2026-04-23: Shell status command with mixed cheap/slow fields — print everything immediately with a "checking…" placeholder for the slow one, then ANSI-rewrite in place when the background `curl` finishes. Three-part pattern: `setopt LOCAL_OPTIONS NO_MONITOR NO_NOTIFY` at function top silences zsh's `[N] PID / [N] Done` job-control noise; spawn `(slow > $tmp) &` + `wait $pid`; rewrite with `\033[nA\r\033[K<line>\033[nB\r` (up n, col 0, clear, reprint, down n). Guard the ANSI dance behind `[[ -t 1 ]]` so pipes/non-TTY get the blocking render. macOS `mktemp -t <prefix>` needs explicit `.XXXXXXXX` suffix; bare prefix errors "too few X's". Example: `ws wg status` egress field in dotfiles ws.zsh.
- [2026-04-23-nix-darwin-launchdaemon-nix-store-boot-race.md](2026-04-23-nix-darwin-launchdaemon-nix-store-boot-race.md) — 2026-04-23: On macOS with Determinate Nix, a `launchd.daemons.*` plist whose `ProgramArguments[0]` is a `/nix/store/.../bin/foo` path silently fails to auto-load at boot — launchd scans `/Library/LaunchDaemons/` before `/nix/store` is synthesized via firmlink, no log entry, daemon just skipped. Plist is valid, not disabled, `launchctl list | grep <label>` returns empty. Fix: entrypoint must live on `/` — use `/bin/bash -c` with a 60s polling wait for `/run/current-system/sw/bin/<tool>` then `exec`. Matches the pattern already used by in-repo nix-darwin LaunchAgents.
- [2026-04-22-intellij-mcp-sse-port-plus-1000.md](2026-04-22-intellij-mcp-sse-port-plus-1000.md) — 2026-04-22: IntelliJ 2026.1's MCP Server plugin dropped the legacy `/api/mcp/list_tools` paths that `@jetbrains/mcp-proxy` (the official stdio shim) still polls — it now speaks standard MCP SSE on builtin-webserver-port + 1000 (63342 → 64342) at `/sse`. Symptom: Claude Code registers the `jetbrains` server cleanly, proxy launches with no errors, zero tools exposed. Fix: drop the shim, configure `.mcp.json` with `{"type":"sse","url":"http://127.0.0.1:64342/sse"}` directly. Generalizable: when an MCP server registers cleanly but exposes zero tools, verify the server's reachable on its *current* transport before debugging the shim — plugin authors migrate transports faster than their proxy packages.
- [2026-04-22-intellij-bundledkeymap-bare-filename.md](2026-04-22-intellij-bundledkeymap-bare-filename.md) — 2026-04-22: IntelliJ `<bundledKeymap file="X.xml" />` must use a BARE filename (no `/keymaps/` path prefix). The extension derives the keymap's registered name from the filename minus `.xml` — the XML `<keymap name="...">` attribute is ignored for registration. Declaring `file="/keymaps/Foo.xml"` silently registers under name `/keymaps/Foo` (both `getName()` and `getPresentableName()`), so `KeymapManagerEx.setActiveKeymap` lookups by the XML name fail with no obvious error. Fix: rename resource to match the desired display name (spaces allowed) and declare `file="Foo Bar.xml"` — matches IntelliJ's own Eclipse/NetBeans keymap plugins. Diagnostic: log `allKeymaps.joinToString { "${it.presentableName} (${it.name})" }` — wrongly-registered entries show as `/keymaps/Foo (/keymaps/Foo)`.
- [2026-04-22-macos-killall-silent-noop-apple-daemons.md](2026-04-22-macos-killall-silent-noop-apple-daemons.md) — 2026-04-22: `sudo killall UniversalControl` on macOS 15+ silently no-ops — reports success, PID/uptime unchanged. Default SIGTERM is dropped by some SIP-protected Apple daemons (UC, rapportd, bluetoothd, sharingd…). Use `sudo pkill -9 -x <name>` to force-kill and let launchd respawn. Verify with `pgrep -x` / `ps -p <pid>`: if PID didn't change, the signal never landed.
- [2026-04-22-resilience-patterns-for-any-codebase.md](2026-04-22-resilience-patterns-for-any-codebase.md) — 2026-04-22: Portable checklist of resilience/performance patterns that apply to any backend/service/agent codebase — retry with backoff, batch DB writes, idempotency via unique index + ON CONFLICT, rate limiting, timeouts, context propagation, singleflight, cache invalidation on rejection, per-item failure aggregation, cost-of-scale math before shipping. Automated code reviewers don't catch their absence because they check defects in what's there, not missing idioms. Techniques: diff against the sibling implementation, explicit self-review against the list, dogfood the error path (kill network/DB locally).
- [2026-04-22-zellij-action-rename-session.md](2026-04-22-zellij-action-rename-session.md) — 2026-04-22: Zellij has a true in-place session rename — `zellij -s <old> action rename-session <new>` — hidden under the `action` subcommand (top-level `zellij --help` shows only kill/delete). Preserves panes/tabs/scrollback; targets detached sessions without attaching. Bonus gotcha: session names cap at ~24 chars on macOS (unix-socket path limit); zellij's validator underflows to the nonsense "session name must be less than 0 characters" — pre-check length yourself.
- [2026-04-21-macos-screenshot-nnbsp-filename.md](2026-04-21-macos-screenshot-nnbsp-filename.md) — 2026-04-21: macOS screenshot filenames use U+202F (NARROW NO-BREAK SPACE) between the time and "PM"/"AM", not ASCII space — `cp "Screenshot ... 2.27.53 PM.png"` fails with "No such file" even when the file is there. Detect via `ls | cat -A` (shows `M-bM-^@M-/`); fix via glob pattern or `$'\u202f'` literal.
- [2026-04-21-rust-test-only-dep-dev-deps.md](2026-04-21-rust-test-only-dep-dev-deps.md) — 2026-04-21: Rust test-only deps (used under `#[cfg(test)]`) MUST live in `[dev-dependencies]`, not `[dependencies]`.
